title: Encastra component manifest
description: DOCUMENTATION, NOT THE AUTHORITY. This schema exists so that an author's editor can autocomplete and catch obvious mistakes early. The runtime's own validator (crates/encastra-protocol/src/manifest.rs) is what decides whether a manifest is acceptable, and it enforces rules a JSON Schema cannot express — that every port type resolves in the type graph, that every declared capability is one this build can actually enforce, and that no floating-point number appears anywhere in the document. Passing this schema does not mean a manifest will load.

schema.description: Protocol revision. Additive-only. A host refuses a value it does not know rather than guessing.

id.description: Reverse-DNS, at least two segments, e.g. "encastra.image.resize". Immutable for the life of the component.

version.description: Semver. Immutable once published: the registry refuses different bytes under the same id@version.

runtime.description: Semver range of host versions this component is known to work on, e.g. ">=0.4.0 <2.0.0".

kind.description: "core" is first-party and compiled into the host. Anything published by a third party is "wasm" and runs sandboxed with no ambient authority.

capabilities.description: Ask for the least you can. Every entry beyond an "input-handles" scope puts a question in front of the user, and a component that asks for more than it needs is one people decline.

retryable.description: Whether a failed run is safe to repeat automatically. Leave this false unless the component is genuinely idempotent — retrying a POST or a write is worse than failing once.

type.description: A type expression: a named type, list<T>, or option<T>. The runtime checks that it resolves; this schema only checks the shape.

default.description: Integers only, never a decimal — the manifest's canonical bytes are what get signed, and float formatting is the one part of that nobody agrees on.

kind.description: Only capabilities the host can enforce exist. Process execution and raw device access are absent from this list, not merely denied.

scope.description: "input-handles" means "only what the graph wired to my ports" and needs no decision from the user. Anything wider does.

reason.description: Shown verbatim in the consent dialog. Write it for the person deciding, not for the reviewer: "Uploads the finished image to the URL you configure", not "network access required".
